This relay detects the fault 
 on the bus bar and trips all breakers connected to the bus. Type PVD relays 
 are single phase high speed high impedance voltage operated relays that are 
 designed to provide protection in bus differential schemes when used in 
 junction with suitable current transformers. This model includes a high 
 speed over current unit ( 87H ) in addition to the voltage-operated unit ( 
 87L ). It is provided with a single seal in and separate targets for each 
 unit.

items:
Switch off 
 DC power supply before with drawing the relay.
Test leads, and test plug handle.

Obtain copy of relay setting 
 from field maintenance file.

Obtain outage for the bus bar 
 which is protected by this relay.

Make sure CT secondary circuits are 
 shorted before isolating the relay current circuit for current injection.

Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 3 and 4 ) on phase R of 
 the relay.

Increase the current until the instantaneous unit 87H picks up and the target 
 operates.
Record the current value in the test sheet.

Connect test leads between the voltage terminals ( 5 and 6 ). This relay 
 operates at the high voltage tap which from ( 200 v 500 v ).

Change the voltage scale at the first tap and increase the voltage until the 
 relay trips .
Record the voltage value in the test sheet.
Repeat the steps no. 5 , 6 at the second voltage tap.
Repeat the above steps from 1 to 7 for the other phases S & T .
Repeat all the steps of BUS 1 to BUS 2

Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the 
 test leads from the relay terminal block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads from the terminals ( 3 - 4 ) 
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact ( 5 - 6 ).

Make sure CT and PT secondary circuits 
 are in normal condition.
Remove the isolation from the bus bar.

Introduction
This document outlines the testing procedure I1, which must be performed on an 
annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above title block
This relay detects the fault 
 on the bus bar and trips all breakers connected to the bus. Type PVD relays 
 are single phase high speed high impedance voltage operated relays that are 
 designed to provide protection in bus differential schemes when used in 
 junction with suitable current transformers. This model includes a high 
 speed over current unit ( 87H ) in addition to the voltage-operated unit ( 
 87L ). It is provided with a single seal in and separate targets for each 
 unit.

Safety Precautions

Tools and Equipment
Secondary injection test set,

Work to be Carried Out
Preparation
Obtain copy of relay setting 
 from field maintenance file.
Obtain outage for the bus bar 
 which is protected by this relay.
Make sure CT secondary circuits are 
 shorted before isolating the relay current circuit for current injection.
Test 
Procedure 
BUS ( 1 )
Connect test leads between the current terminals ( 3 and 4 ) on phase R of 
 the relay.
Increase the current until the instantaneous unit 87H picks up and the target 
 operates.
Record the current value in the test sheet.
Connect test leads between the voltage terminals ( 5 and 6 ). This relay 
 operates at the high voltage tap which from ( 200 v 500 v ).
Change the voltage scale at the first tap and increase the voltage until the 
 relay trips .
Record the voltage value in the test sheet.
Repeat the steps no. 5 , 6 at the second voltage tap.
Repeat the above steps from 1 to 7 for the other phases S & T .
BUS ( 2 )
Repeat all the steps of BUS 1 to BUS 2
Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service
Return relay to service by removing the 
 test leads from the relay terminal block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads from the terminals ( 3 - 4 ) 
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact ( 5 - 6 ).
Make sure CT and PT secondary circuits 
 are in normal condition.
Remove the isolation from the bus bar.
